docs.title: MatCore
docs.text:
Material Core (MatCore) is a metadata standard for computational materials science. MatCore represents key aspects of a material-focused computation to make it understandable to the broad materials research community. It provides pragmatic and workable guidelines for documentation of materials data.

MatCore is developed as a grassroots effort by experts in first principles calculations, molecular dynamics, phase field, machine learning for materials, and related fields.

The MatCore effort is funded by the National Science Foundation, Division of Materials Research (DMR) through Award #2404283 and supported through the KIM Initiative.

docs.title: About MatCore
docs.text: The Material Core Metadata (MatCore) standard for computational materials science (CMS) represents key aspects of a material-focused computation to make it understandable to the broad materials research community. It provides pragmatic and workable guidelines for documentation of materials data.

docs.title: Goals
docs.text:
The primary goals of the MatCore standard are, by outlining expectations for metadata accompanying a computational dataset, to facilitate:

  • Dataset transparency, discoverability, sharing and reuse in theoretical and computational modeling.
  • Verification and validation of materials modeling and simulation software.
  • Training physics-based and machine learning models for material behavior.
  • Promote reproducibility in CMS by providing the information necessary for researchers to regenerate a published dataset.

docs.title: Scope
docs.text:
The MatCore standard is focused on CMS methods aimed at computing material properties from a microscopic perspective, as opposed to computational methods in which the material is a component (such as engineering finite element analysis). The MatCore standard is designed to be flexible so that it can be extended to any area of CMS and can accommodate future changes in the field. An initial focus is placed on major CMS methods most widely used at the time of the creation of the standard with the aim of adding other methods in the future. The initial methods to be supported are:

  • Density functional theory
  • Many-body perturbation theory (GW, BSE)
  • Machine learning for materials
  • Molecular dynamics
  • Phase field
  • Derived approaches involving a combination of other methods

docs.title: Standard
docs.text: All methods share a common minimal set of metadata defined by the MatCore standard. The minimal MatCore metadata includes aspects of a dataset deemed important to report for data findability and reuse and are universal across all computational methods. In addition, each method has its own MatCore extension, e.g. MatCore-MD, MatCore-DFT, etc., that inherits from the minimal MatCore metadata and adds additional method-specific metadata.

docs.title: 1. Preamble
docs.text:
Material Core Metadata (MatCore) Standard

Version 0.5.0

docs.title: 1.1 Objectives
docs.text:
The Material Core Metadata (MatCore) standard for computational materials science (CMS) represents key aspects of a material-focused computation to make it understandable to the broad materials research community. It provides pragmatic and workable guidelines for documentation of materials data.

The primary goals of the MatCore standard are, by outlining expectations for metadata accompanying a computational dataset, to facilitate: (1) dataset transparency, discoverability, sharing and reuse in theoretical and computational modeling, (2) verification and validation of materials modeling and simulation software, and (3) training physics-based and machine learning (ML) models for material behavior. An additional, more challenging, objective is to promote reproducibility in CMS by providing the information necessary for researchers to regenerate a published dataset.

docs.title: 1.2 Scope
docs.text:
The MatCore standard is focused on CMS methods aimed at computing material properties from a microscopic perspective, as opposed to computational methods in which the material is a component (such as engineering finite element analysis). The MatCore standard is designed to be flexible so that it can be extended to any area of CMS and can accommodate future changes in the field. An initial focus is placed on major CMS methods most widely used at the time of the creation of the standard with the aim of adding other methods in the future. The initial methods to be supported are:

  • DFT: Density functional theory

  • MD: Classical molecular dynamics

  • MBPT: Many-body perturbation theory (GW/BSE)

  • ML: Machine learning

  • PF: Phase field

  • DER: Derived properties from CMS calculations

All methods share a common minimal set of metadata defined by the MatCore standard. In addition, each method has its own MatCore extension, e.g. MatCore-DFT, MatCore-MD, etc., that inherits from the minimal MatCore metadata and adds additional method-specific metadata.

It is allowable to include multiple method-specific metadata if used in concert. For example, an ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) dataset could include both MatCore-DFT and MatCore-MD metadata files to document both aspects of the computation.

docs.title: 1.3 Format
docs.text:
Each standard consists of a set of Properties with possible SubProperties, SubSubProperties, etc. The term “Property” will be used in the rest of this section to refer collectively to Property, SubProperty, etc. Properties have the following characteristics:

  • Each Property has a name consisting of a series of one or more words all in lower case separated by hyphens.

  • Required Properties are indicated by an asterisk (*) appended to the end of the Property name.

  • Properties have the following features:

    • Definition: A short explanation of the nature of the Property. Best-practice is to not use words from the Property name in the definition to prevent circular definitions, except in cases where confusion is unlikely.

    • Type: The data type of the Property's value: string, float, int, bool, file, or any (the instance states the type). A Property that only contains SubProperties has no type.

    • Extent: The shape of the value, in KIM notation: [] for a scalar, [3,3] for a 3×3 array, [:] for a list of any length, or any when the schema does not fix it.

    • Values: The values the Property can take on, such as a controlled vocabulary, bounds, a format or a pattern, with examples.

      • When appropriate a controlled vocabulary can be defined. In this case sentence case format is adopted (i.e. for a phrase containing several words, the first letter of the first word is capitalized and all others are lower case except for proper names or acronyms). An option should always be added for users to add terms not included in the controlled vocabulary to allow the standard to support future developments. New terms may eventually be standardized and added to the controlled vocabulary.

      • When a controlled vocabulary is used, adoption of existing standards is recommended whenever possible.

      • A Property either has a value of its own or has SubProperties, never both. A numerical value (a value whose Kind is not "inapplicable") is therefore a Property with two SubProperties, value and unit. In the Standard, value defines the Type, Extent, Kind and Recommended unit of the quantity. In a metadata instance, value holds the quantity and unit holds the unit in which it is expressed; unit SHALL be given, and SHALL be a symbol from the MatCore Unit Table (Annex U) whose Kind is compatible with the Kind of value. A property value without a unit, or with a unit incompatible with its Kind, is non-conformant; no default unit is ever implied. The Recommended unit listed for each property is informative and does not affect how values are interpreted. A pure number (a ratio, a fraction or a count) takes the same form: its Kind is dimensionless, and its unit is the reserved symbol dimensionless, the only symbol of that Kind. The same symbol is used wherever a unit is given for a pure number, as in a generic parameter or a nondimensional length. Plane angles use an angle unit (rad or degree). Where the meaning of a value depends on a convention that a unit cannot express (e.g. inclusion of a factor 2π in reciprocal lengths, or components given in a lattice basis), the property has a convention or basis subproperty, required as stated in its description. Some units (bohr, hartree, Ry) are defined through measured physical constants, so their values in SI units change slightly each time CODATA revises those constants; MatCore uses the CODATA 2022 values listed in Annex U.

      • A generic parameter holds a parameter whose meaning the Standard does not fix, such as a parameter of an exchange-correlation functional. It is a Property with four SubProperties, in this order: name (required), the designation of the parameter; value (required), whose Type, Extent and Kind are any, the metadata instance stating its type (float, int, string or bool) and its unit; unit (required), a symbol from the MatCore Unit Table (Annex U), the reserved symbol dimensionless, or, if and only if no Annex U symbol applies, a string prefixed x-gnu: giving a GNU Units expression (accepted with a validation warning); and description (optional), an explanation of the parameter.

      • A Property that contains SubProperties shows them nested within it.

    • Kind: The physical dimension of the Property's value, given as a MatCore Kind name mapped to a QUDT QuantityKind IRI in Annex U (e.g. Energy, Length, InverseLength, Temperature, Pressure). Reserved values: dimensionless (ratios, counts), inapplicable (strings, identifiers, and the unit subproperty itself), any (the value of a generic name/value/unit parameter, whose Kind is then given by the instance unit).

    • Recommended unit: The unit customarily used for this Property in the community. Informative only; used by templates and tools.

    • Repeatable: A boolean variable that is “True” for Properties that may appear multiple times inside the metadata file. For example, for a dataset created by more than one person, the creator Property can be repeated as many times as needed, each with its own SubProperties.

    • Note(s): Additional clarifying information regarding a Property.

In addition to the required and optional Properties, other arbitrary Properties can be added to any MatCore Standard metadata files to support developments in the field. Such Properties may eventually be standardized and added to the MatCore Standard.

Examples are provided after each Standard specification in XML format. However, this is for clarification purposes only. The MatCore Standard serves as a conceptual and logical framework. It defines the schema for Properties required to ensure data consistency and interoperability. Critically, the MatCore Standard is implementation-agnostic. It dictates what information must be captured and how it should be structured logically, but it does not mandate a specific substrate, file format, or programming language.

A serialization is a file format (for example XML or JSON) together with the rules that map the MatCore data model onto it.

MatCore adopts Semantic Versioning (SemVer) three-part versioning system (major, minor, patch) to indicate Standard changes.

* required appears at most once repeatable

A primary entity (e.g. person, organization, software agent) responsible for creating the dataset's core content and their institutional affiliation if relevant.

Required Repeatable yes yes name*

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable —

Examples: Albert Einstein, Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory, Claude Opus 5.5.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [:] inapplicable —

A description of a computer simulation used to generate data in the dataset.

The general category to which the computational technique belongs.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable —

docs.title: 2.2 Density Functional Theory (DFT) Metadata
docs.text:
Version 0.5.0

The metadata for density functional theory (DFT) data (MatCore-DFT) is tabulated below. This includes the level of theory (exchange-correlation functional, core-electron model, and valence-electron model) and associated parameters. (Note: This standard inherits the metadata in the minimal MatCore standard, adding the properties below.)

* required appears at most once repeatable

xc-functional*

Approximation used to describe the electron exchange and electron correlation energies

Required Repeatable yes yes type*

The mathematical form of the exchange-correlation functional.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable —

Recommended: LDA, GGA, Meta GGA, Hybrid, ML. Other values are allowed. "LDA" – Local Density Approximation. "GGA" – Generalized Gradient Approximation. "Meta GGA" – Extension to GGA including dependence on Laplacian of electron density. "Hybrid" – An approximation for the exchange-correlation (XC) functional that includes a portion of the exact XC from Hartree–Fock theory or machine learning with the rest coming from other sources (ab initio or empirical). "ML" – Machine learning based functional.

description

Explanatory text providing more information about the type of the exchange-correlation method used including any relevant identifying information.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no string [] inapplicable —

Examples of possible content by type: LDA: Common parameterizations: VWN, PW92, etc. GGA: Typical choices are PW91, PBE, rPBE, revPBE, BLYP, etc. Meta GGA: Specific named examples include TPSS, SCAN, M06, etc. Hybrid: B3LYP, PBE0, HSE03, HSE06, NeuralXC, DeePKS, … ML: DM21, NNLDA, NNGGA, CIDER, etc. Others: BEEF, VdW-corrections (added on top of XC, e.g., D2, D3, D4), etc. LibXC designation: LibXC:LDA_C_GK72 (include source as prefix).

xc-parameter

A fixed variable associated with the specified exchange-correlation functional method.

Required Repeatable no yes

Note: For example, the mixing parameter of a hybrid exchange-correlation functional, or another method-specific parameter.

name*

The designation of the exchange-correlation parameter.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable — value*

The data associated with the exchange-correlation parameter.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no any any any — unit*

The unit in which the associated value is expressed.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable —

A symbol from the MatCore Unit Table (Annex U), or the reserved symbol dimensionless. If and only if no Annex U symbol applies, a string prefixed x-gnu: giving a GNU Units expression (accepted with a validation warning).

description

An explanation of the meaning, source, or purpose of the parameter.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no string [] inapplicable — core-electron-model*

Model of the electrons used in the calculation.

Required Repeatable yes no type*

The method used to model the electrons.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable —

Recommended: All Electron, LAPW, Pseudopotential, PAW. Other values are allowed. "All Electron" – All of the electrons in an atom are modeled explicitly. "LAPW" – Linearized Augmented Plane Wave. "Pseudopotential" – Valence electrons are treated explicitly, and core electrons are modeled by a simplified potential. "PAW" – Projector Augmented Wave.

pseudopotential

For type "Pseudopotential", or type "PAW", additional information about the pseudopotentials.

Required Repeatable no yes name*

The name of the pseudopotential.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable — type*

The physical form of the pseudopotential.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable —

Recommended: Norm conserving, Ultrasoft. Other values are allowed.

description

Explanatory text about the pseudopotential including any relevant identifying information.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no string [] inapplicable — number-of-valence-electrons*

The number of electrons treated explicitly.

Required Repeatable yes no value*

The value of the property, in the unit given by unit.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no int [] dimensionless dimensionless

Minimum: 1.

unit*

The unit of the value, an Annex U symbol whose Kind is the Kind of value.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable —

The only allowed unit is dimensionless.

repository

The database from which the pseudopotential was obtained.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no string [] inapplicable — version

The version of the pseudopotential.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no string [] inapplicable —

Examples: 6.3.1.

doi

The digital object identifier (DOI) for the pseudopotential.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no string [] inapplicable —

Pattern: https://doi\.org/10\.[^/]+/.+.

checksum

A digital fingerprint of the pseudopotential file, computed by a named algorithm.

Required Repeatable no no

Note: Use checksum when the pseudopotential is identified by a checksum of its file (e.g. the SHA256 hash of a VASP POTCAR file). For any other designation, use unique-identifier.

file*

The name of the file.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable — algorithm*

The algorithm that computed the checksum.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable —

Recommended: SHA1, SHA224, SHA256, SHA384, SHA512, SHA3-256, SHA3-384, SHA3-512, BLAKE2b-256, BLAKE2b-384, BLAKE2b-512, BLAKE3, MD2, MD4, MD5, MD6, ADLER32. Other values are allowed. The algorithm names of SPDX 2.3.1 §8.4 (File checksum field).

value*

The checksum of the file, in lowercase hexadecimal digits.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable —

Pattern: [0-9a-f]+.

unique-identifier

A token other than a checksum that identifies the pseudopotential, such as a label or code assigned by the library that distributes it.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no string [] inapplicable —

Note: For a checksum of the pseudopotential file, use checksum instead.

valence-electron-model*

The elementary functions used for expanding electronic wave functions.

Required Repeatable yes no type*

The choice of a basis set to expand electronic wave functions.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes yes string [] inapplicable —

Recommended: Plane waves, LAPW, Localized orbitals, PAW. Other values are allowed. "LAPW" – Linearized Augmented Plane Wave.

localized-orbital-basis-set

For type "Localized orbitals", additional information about the localized orbital basis set.

Required Repeatable no yes type*

The designation of the set of orbital functions used for expanding electronic wave functions.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable —

Examples: 6-31G, DZP.

repository

The database from which the localized-orbital basis set was obtained.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no string [] inapplicable — version

The version of the localized-orbital basis set.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no string [] inapplicable — doi

The digital object identifier (DOI) for the localized-orbital basis set.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no string [] inapplicable —

Pattern: https://doi\.org/10\.[^/]+/.+.

checksum

A digital fingerprint of the localized-orbital basis set file, computed by a named algorithm.

Required Repeatable no no

Note: Use checksum when the basis set is identified by a checksum of its file. For any other designation, use unique-identifier.

file*

The name of the file.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable — algorithm*

The algorithm that computed the checksum.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable —

Recommended: SHA1, SHA224, SHA256, SHA384, SHA512, SHA3-256, SHA3-384, SHA3-512, BLAKE2b-256, BLAKE2b-384, BLAKE2b-512, BLAKE3, MD2, MD4, MD5, MD6, ADLER32. Other values are allowed. The algorithm names of SPDX 2.3.1 §8.4 (File checksum field).

value*

The checksum of the file, in lowercase hexadecimal digits.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable —

Pattern: [0-9a-f]+.

unique-identifier

A token other than a checksum that identifies the localized-orbital basis set, such as a label or code assigned by the library that distributes it.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no string [] inapplicable —

Note: For a checksum of the basis set file, use checksum instead.

kinetic-energy-cutoff

For type not "Localized orbitals", the maximum kinetic energy of the plane waves included in the calculation of wave functions.

Required Repeatable no no value*

The value of the property, in the unit given by unit.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no float [] Energy eV

Minimum: 0.

unit*

The unit of the value, an Annex U symbol whose Kind is the Kind of value.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable — charge-density-cutoff

For type not "Localized orbitals", the energy value used to truncate the plane wave expansion of the electron charge density.

Required Repeatable no no value*

The value of the property, in the unit given by unit.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no float [] Energy eV

Minimum: 0.

unit*

The unit of the value, an Annex U symbol whose Kind is the Kind of value.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable — calculation-physics

Additional phenomena included beyond the standard DFT calculation.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no yes — — — —

Legacy: String containing one of the following values: "Relativistic effects" "Spin polarization" "Noncollinear spin polarization" "On-site correlation" (e.g. DFT+U) "Van der Waals" Other user-specified value if none of the above apply.

k-point-mesh

For periodic systems, a grid of points sampled within the Brillouin zone, used to approximate integrals and calculate electronic properties by discretizing the wavefunction across reciprocal space.

Required Repeatable no no type*

The choice of how k-points are distributed on the mesh.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no — — — —

Legacy: String containing one of the following values: "Monkhorst-Pack" "Gamma centered" "Irregular" Other user-specified value if none of the above apply.

number-of-points

How many k-points are included along each reciprocal lattice vector.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no — — — —

Legacy: Ordered list of three integer numbers containing the number k-points along the three reciprocal lattice vector directions. Legacy unit: dimensionless

k-point-spacing

Separation between k-points along each reciprocal lattice vector direction.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no — — — —

Legacy: Real number containing the k-point spacing. Legacy unit: 1/angstrom (1/Å)

State whether the factor 2π is included in the reciprocal length.

shift

Translation of the k-point mesh along the reciprocal lattice vector directions.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no — — — —

Legacy: Ordered list of three real numbers containing the shifts along the three reciprocal lattice vector directions. Legacy unit: 1/angstrom (1/Å)

smearing-type

The choice of method for assigning fractional occupancies of electronic states and/or facilitating reciprocal space integrations.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no — — — —

Legacy: String containing one of the following values: "None" "None - tetrahedron" "None - Blöchl-corrected tetrahedron" "Gaussian" "Fermi" "Methfessel-Paxton" Other user-specified value if none of the above apply.

smearing-width

A parameter that controls the broadening of the electron energy levels near the Fermi level.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no — — — —

Legacy: Real number containing the smearing width. Legacy unit: electron Volt (eV)

methfessel-paxton-order

For smearing-type "Methfessel-Paxton", level of polynomial approximation used in the Methfessel-Paxton smearing method

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no — — — —

Legacy: Integer containing the Methfessel-Paxton order. Legacy unit: dimensionless

self-consistent-field-convergence

Method and termination criteria defining the precision of self-consistent solution of the Kohn-Sham equations.

Required Repeatable no no method

The self-consistent field mixing and/or extrapolation scheme for the iterative solution of the Kohn-Sham equations.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no — — — —

Legacy: String containing one of the following values: "Simple mixing" "Pulay mixing" "Blocked Davidson" "DIIS" – Direct Inversion in the Iterative Subspace "BFGS" – Broyden–Fletcher–Goldfarb–Shanno algorithm Other user-specified value if none of the above apply.

tolerance*

Convergence criterion (on total energy) for the self-consistent loop.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no — — — —

Legacy: Real number containing the convergence tolerance Legacy unit: electron Volt (eV)

relaxation-tolerance-energy

Total energy convergence criterion for atomic relaxation.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no — — — —

Legacy: Real number containing the convergence tolerance Legacy unit: electron Volt (eV)

relaxation-tolerance-forces

Maximum force convergence criterion for atomic relaxation.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no — — — —

Legacy: Real number containing the convergence tolerance Legacy unit: electron Volt (eV/Å)

comment

Additional information on the DFT calculation. For example, non-self-consistent constraints, such as details about imposed state occupation or moment freezing.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no yes — — — —

Legacy: String containing the calculation comments.

docs.title: 2.3 Molecular Dynamics (MD) Metadata
docs.text:
Version 0.5.0

The metadata for classical molecular dynamics (MD) data (MatCore-MD) is tabulated below. This category includes energy and free energy minimization, equilibrium and nonequilibrium MD, and related approaches. (Note: This standard inherits the metadata in the minimal MatCore standard, adding the properties below.)

* required appears at most once repeatable

computation*

The form of molecular dynamics performed.

Required Repeatable yes yes mode*

The type of the molecular dynamics simulation performed.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no — — — —

Legacy: String containing one of the following values: "Static" – Snapshot(s) of arbitrary particle configuration "Minimization" – Energy minimization "Equilibrium dynamics" – Equilibrium molecular dynamics "Nonequilibrium dynamics" – Nonequilibrium molecular dynamics. "Free energy" – Free energy calculations Other user-specified value if none of the above apply.

algorithm

The computational method used to perform the computation.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no — — — —

Legacy: String containing one of the following values based on the specified calculation type:: For "Minimization": "Simplex" "Damped dynamics" "FIRE" "Steepest descent" "Conjugate gradients" "BFGS" "Simulated annealing" "SGLD" – Stochastic Gradient Langevin Dynamics Other user-specified value if none of the above apply. For "Equilibrium dynamics" or "nonequilibrium-dynamics": "Leap frog" "Runge-Kutta" "Velocity Verlet" "Verlet" Other user-specified value if none of the above apply. For "Free energy": "Harmonic" "Metadynamics" "PMF" – Potential of Mean Force "Thermodynamic integration" "Umbrella sampling" Other user-specified value if none of the above apply.

computation-parameter

A fixed variable associated with the specified computation algorithm.

Required Repeatable no yes name*

The designation of the parameter associated with the specified computation algorithm.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no — — — —

Legacy: A string containing the name of the computation parameter.

value*

The data associated with the computation parameter.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no — — — —

Legacy: An integer, real, boolean, or string containing the computation parameter value.

unit*

A standardized string or identifier that defines the dimension or measurement system of the associated value.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no — — — —

Legacy: A string containing the units of the value in the GNU unit convention (or the text "dimensionless").

description

An explanation of the meaning, source, or purpose of the computation parameter.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no — — — —

Legacy: A string explaining the computation parameter (e.g. "The convergence tolerance for energy minimization", "The simulation time for the dynamical simulation").

initialization

Information on the conditions set at the start of the simulation.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no — — — —

Legacy: String containing a description of the simulation initial conditions (such as the nature and source of an initial structure, initialization of velocities or spins, etc.).

particle-style*

The nature of the discrete entities used in the molecular dynamics simulation.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no — — — —

Legacy: String containing one of the following values: "Atom" – Each particle represents an individual atom "Radical" – Each particle represents a free radical "United atom" – Each particle represents a fixed grouping of atoms "Bead" – Each particle represents a user-tuneable group of atoms "Coarse grained" – Each particle represents a higher scale particle obtained by scaling up the atomic representation "Mesoscale" – Granular particles used to simulate microstructure at the mesoscopic scale "Classical electron" – Antisymmetrized wave packet representation of valence electrons Other user-specified value if none of the above apply.

particle-interactions*

The model used to describe the potential energy surface of the system.

Required Repeatable yes yes

Note: This field can be repeated in cases where there are multiple interaction models used in the same simulation (e.g. hybrid calculations combining multiple models or QM/MM style computations).

model-type*

The kind of potential used to compute the particle interactions.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no — — — —

Legacy: A string containing the model type (e.g. Lennard-Jones, EAM, MACE, etc.).

bonding-type*

Specifies whether the bonds between particles are immutable or can be broken.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no — — — —

Legacy: String containing one of the following values: "Reactive" – Bonds formed or broken on-the-fly based on the particle environment "Bonded fixed" – Bonds defined *a priori *and cannot be broken during the simulation. "Bonded mutable" – Bonds defined *a priori *but can be broken and/or formed during the simulation. Other user-specified value if none of the above apply.

theory-level*

The rigor with which the atomic interactions are modeled.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no — — — —

Legacy: String containing one of the following values: "Classical physics-based" – Electronic degrees of freedom subsumed into a model of atomic bonding "Classical machine-learning" – Machine learning model trained to take particle positions as input "Tight-binding" – Classical model of nuclear interactions with approximate treatment of the electrons "Ab initio" – Some level of electronic structure determines the particle interactions "Ab initio machine learning" – Machine learning model employing some level of electronic structure in determining the particle interactions Other user-specified value if none of the above apply.

source

Information that uniquely identifies the origin of the particle interaction model (e.g. a journal article, or a repository containing an implementation or parameter set).

Required Repeatable no yes reference*

The origin of the particle interaction model implementation used, such as an interatomic potential repository (e.g. OpenKIM or the NIST IPR), a code (like LAMMPS), or a publication.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no — — — —

Legacy: String containing the name of the source and other identifying information (e.g. journal citation, repository and unique identifier in the repository)

doi

The digital object identifier (DOI) for the source.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no — — — —

Legacy: A string containing the source DOI.

link

A URI pointing to a permanent location of the source.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no — — — —

Legacy: A string containing the file URI.

charge-interactions

The model used to describe the interactions between charged particles.

Required Repeatable no yes charge-origin*

Nature of the particle charges.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no — — — —

Legacy: String containing one of the following values: "Semi empirical" – Charges obtained from semi-empirical quantum calculations "Quantum" – Charges obtained from quantum calculations "Electronic population" – Charges obtained from electronic population analysis, e.g. Mulliken "Electronegativity" – Charges obtained from electronegativity differences between atoms "Tabulated" – Charges obtained from an external source Other user-specified value if none of the above apply.

charge-style*

The nature of the charges associated with the particles, such as total or effective charges.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no — — — —

Legacy: String containing one of the following values: "Coulomb full" – The particle charge accounting for all electrons "Coulomb screened" – Effective charge due to screening or shielding by other electrons (e.g. Slater) Other user-specified value if none of the above apply.

charge-variability*

Attribute specifying the method for dynamically varying the local electric charge associated with discrete entities.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no — — — —

Legacy: String containing one of the following values: "Fixed" – Charges cannot change during the simulation "QEq" – Charge equilibration method "EEM" – Electronegativity Equalization Method "iEL/SCF" – Extended Lagrangian/self-consistent field scheme "FlucQ" – Fluctuating charge potential "Drude" – Drude method Other user-specified value if none of the above apply.

long-range-electrostatics

Method used to compute long-range electrostatic interactions.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no — — — —

Legacy: String containing one of the following values: "None" – No electrostatic calculation performed "Direct" – All Coulomb interactions computed directly "Ewald" – Ewald summation "PME" – Particle mesh Ewald "PPPM" – Particle particle particle mesh "Reaction" – Reaction field Other user-specified value if none of the above apply.

electric-dipole

Attribute specifying the type of interaction associated with the local electric dipoles associated with particles.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no — — — —

Legacy: String containing one of the following values: "Stockmayer" – Stockmayer potential "Screened" – Screened dipoles "Long range" – Long-range dipoles Other user-specified value if none of the above apply.

electric-dipole-variability

Attribute specifying the method for dynamically varying the local electric charge associated with discrete entities.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no — — — —

Legacy: String containing one of the following values: "Induced" – Induced point dipoles "Isotropic" – Isotropic polarizability "Anisotropic" – Anisotropic polarizability Other user-specified value if none of the above apply.

magnetic-interactions

The model used to describe the interactions between magnetic spins.

Required Repeatable no yes spin-style*

The nature of the magnetic spins associated with the particles.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no — — — —

Legacy: String containing one of the following values: "Classical spin dynamics" – Spins modeled as classical vectors evolved via Landau–Lifshitz–Gilbert (LLG) equation defined by a spin Hamiltonian. "Coupled spin lattice dynamics" – Combines classical spin-dynamics with classical molecular dynamics"Ab initio spin dynamics" – Magnetism treated via spin-polarized density functional theory (DFT) "Tight binding spin dynamics" – Magnetism emerges from itinerant electrons rather than fixed local moments "Quantum spin dynamics" – Magnetic moments treated as fully quantum mechanical operators evolving under the time-dependent Schrödinger equation

magnetic-dipole

Attribute specifying the type of interaction (spin Hamiltonian) between the magnetic dipoles associated with particles.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no — — — —

Legacy: String containing a description of the approach used to model the magnetic dipoles (e.g. "Heisenberg", "multi-spin", "Zeeman", or some other formulation for the spin Hamiltonian).

thermodynamic-constraint

Macroscopic physical restriction imposed on the simulation, such as a statistical mechanics ensemble.

Required Repeatable no yes system*

The collection of particles to which the constraint is applied.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no — — — —

Legacy: String describing the constrained system (e.g. entire system, or a subset of atoms that are constrained.)

type*

The nature of the imposed thermodynamic constraint.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no — — — —

Legacy: String containing one of the following values: "NVE" – Microcanonical "NVT" – Canonical "μVT" – Grand canonical "NPT" – Isothermal-isobaric "NσT" – Isothermal-isostress "μPT" – Grand isothermal-isobaric "μσT" – Grand isothermal-isostress "NPH" – Isoenthalpic-isobaric "NσH" – Isoenthalpic-isostress Other user-specified value if none of the above apply.

method

The name of the approach used to impose the constraint.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no — — — —

Legacy: String containing one of the following values based on the specified constraint:: For "NVT": "Andersen" "Berendsen" "CSVR" Langevin "Nosé-Hoover" "Nosé-Hoover chain" "Velocity rescaling" Other user-specified value if none of the above apply. For "μVT": "GCMC" – Grand Canonical Monte Carlo Other user-specified value if none of the above apply. For "NPT": "Andersen" "Berendsen" "CauchyStat" "Nosé-Hoover style" "Parrinello-Rahman" Other user-specified value if none of the above apply. For "NσT": "CauchyStat" "Parrinello-Rahman" Other user-specified value if none of the above apply. For "μPT": User-specified value. For "μσT": User-specified value. For "NPH": "Nosé-Hoover style" Other user-specified value if none of the above apply. For "NσH": User-specified value. Otherwise: User-specified value.

description

Explanatory text about the constraint and method used to impose it.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no — — — —

Legacy: A string containing the constraint description.

td-parameter

A fixed variable associated with the specified thermodynamic constraint.

Required Repeatable no yes name*

The designation of the parameter associated with the specified thermodynamic constraint.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no — — — —

Legacy: A string containing the name of the thermodynamic constraint parameter.

value*

The data associated with the thermodynamic constraint parameter.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no — — — —

Legacy: An integer, real, boolean, or string containing the thermodynamic constraint parameter value.

unit*

A standardized string or identifier that defines the dimension or measurement system of the associated value.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no — — — —

Legacy: A string containing the units of the value in the GNU unit convention (or the text "dimensionless").

description

An explanation of the meaning, source, or purpose of the thermodynamic constraint parameter.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no — — — —

Legacy: A string explaining the thermodynamic constraint parameter (e.g. "The damping parameter for the Langevin thermostat").

docs.title: 2.4 Many-Body Perturbation Theory (MBPT) Metadata
docs.text:
Version 0.5.0

The metadata for Many-Body Perturbation Theory (MBPT) data (MatCore-MBPT) is tabulated below. This includes the MBPT method, starting point, dielectric treatment, and associated parameters. (Note: This standard inherits the metadata in the minimal MatCore standard and MatCore-DFT standard, adding the properties below.)

* required appears at most once repeatable

mbpt-method*

The many-body perturbation theory (MBPT) approach used and associated settings.

Required Repeatable yes no type*

The nature of the MBPT calculation performed.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no — — — —

Legacy: String containing one of the following values: "GW" "BSE" "GW/BSE" Other user-specified value if none of the above apply.

self-consistency*

Specifies the level of iterative updating applied to the Green's function (G), the screened Coulomb interaction (W), or the excitonic Hamiltonian during the calculation. This property identifies whether the MBPT equations are solved in a 'one-shot' perturbative manner or through an iterative cycle where the electronic or excitonic quasiparticle states are updated to reach a self-consistent solution.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no — — — —

Legacy: String containing one of the following values depending on the variant of the GW, BSE, or GW/BSE approach used: "G0W0" – One-shot calculation; the G and *W *are constructed using the starting eigenvalues and wavefunctions. "GW0" – Only the Green's function G is updated iteratively, while *W *remains fixed at the *W0 *level "G0W" – Only the screened interaction W is updated iteratively, while G remains fixed at G0 "scGW" – Fully self-consistent GW; bothG* and W are updated iteratively until the quasiparticle energies and/or wavefunctions converge "QSGW" – Quasiparticle self-consistent GW; the starting potential is updated to provide the optimal independent particle basis for the GW expansion "BSE0" – One-shot BSE; the excitonic Hamiltonian is built once using fixed GW quasiparticle energies and screening (W) "scBSE" – Self-consistent BSE; internal refinement of the kernel or energies within the BSE process "evGW+BSE" – Eigenvalue-only self-consistent GW (evGW) used as the starting point for a subsequent BSE calculation "scGW+BSE" – The BSE is solved using the results of a fully self-consistent GW calculation Other user-specified value if none of the above apply.

starting-point*

The density functional theory (DFT) exchange-correlation functional used to generate Kohn-Sham wavefunctions and eigenvalues for the Green's function and the screened Coulomb interaction.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no — — — —

Legacy: String containing one of the following values: "LDA" "GGA" "Meta GGA" "Hybrid GGA" "DFT+U" Other user-specified value if none of the above apply.

dielectric-matrix*

Information on the dielectric matrix used to compute the screened Coulomb interaction W.

Required Repeatable yes no planewave-basis-cutoff

For a planewave code, the basis set cutoff employed for the dielectric matrix. This is the same as the kinetic energy cutoff.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no — — — —

Legacy: A real number containing the cutoff. Legacy unit: Rydberg (Ry)

Note: Specify either "planewave-basis-cutoff" or "localized-orbital-basis-set", but not both.

localized-orbital-basis-set

For local orbital codes, the name of the basis set .

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no — — — —

Legacy: A string containing the name of the atomic orbital basis. (e.g. "cc-pV6Z").

Note: Specify either "planewave-basis-cutoff" or "localized-orbital-basis-set", but not both.

frequency

The method used to handle the frequency dependence of the Green's function, the screened Coulomb interaction, and their product.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no — — — —

Legacy: String containing one of the following values: "Hybertsen-Louie" "Godby-Needs" "Full frequency real axis" "Full frequency imaginary axis" "Contour deformation" "Spacetime" Other user-specified value if none of the above apply.

response-basis-size

For sum-over-states methods, the number of bands used in the sum. For linear-response methods, the number of dielectric eigenvalues.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no — — — —

Legacy: One integer containing the number of bands or eigenvalues. Legacy unit: dimensionless

q-points*

Brillouin zone grid used for sampling the dielectric matrix.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no — — — —

Legacy: Ordered list of 3 integer numbers containing the number points along the three reciprocal lattice vector directions. Legacy unit: dimensionless

coulomb-truncation

Method used to eliminate long-range Coulomb interactions between periodic replicas in supercell calculations.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no — — — —

Legacy: String containing one of the following values: "Ismail-Beigi" "Rozzi" "Spencer-Alavi" Other user-specified value if none of the above apply.

gw-bands

Number of bands for which the GW correction is evaluated.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no — — — —

Legacy: One integer specifying how many bands are corrected, counting from the bottom of the valence bands. Legacy unit: dimensionless

bse-hamiltonian

A collective descriptor for the parameters defining the construction, dimensionality, and solution method of the effective excitonic Bethe-Salpeter Hamiltonian that is being solved in a BSE calculation. It characterizes the Hilbert space size and the physical constraints (momentum and spin) applied during the diagonalization

Required Repeatable no no number-valence-bands

Number of valence bands included in the BSE Hamiltonian.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no — — — —

Legacy: One integer specifying how many valence bands are corrected, counting from the valence band top. Legacy unit: dimensionless

number-conduction-bands

Number of conduction bands included in the BSE Hamiltonian.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no — — — —

Legacy: One integer specifying how many bands are corrected, counting from the conduction band bottom. Legacy unit: dimensionless

k-point-mesh

Brillouin zone grid used for building the BSE Hamiltonian.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no — — — —

Legacy: Ordered list of 3 integer numbers containing the number points along the reciprocal lattice vector directions. Legacy unit: dimensionless

exciton-momentum

Crystal momentum of the exciton in the BSE calculation.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no — — — —

Legacy: Ordered list of 3 real values containing the crystal momentum in fractions of the reciprocal lattice vectors (dimensionless), e.g. [0.5,0.5,1.0]. Legacy unit: dimensionless

exciton-multiplicity

Specification whether the BSE calculation is performed for singlet or triplet excitons.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no — — — —

Legacy: string containing one of the values: "Singlet" "Triplet" Other user-specified value if none of the above apply.

diagonalization

Approximation method used to diagonalize the BSE Hamiltonian.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no — — — —

Legacy: String containing one of the following values: "Tamm-Dancoff" "Full diagonalization" Other user-specified value if none of the above apply.

number-lowest-eigenvalues

Number of lowest eigenvalues computed by solving the BSE Hamiltonian.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no — — — —

Legacy: One integer containing the number of BSE eigenvalues. Legacy unit: dimensionless

bse-kernel-truncation

Method used to eliminate long-range Coulomb interactions between periodic replicas in the BSE Coulomb kernel.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no — — — —

Legacy: String containing one of the following values: "Ismail-Beigi" "Rozzi" "Spencer-Alavi" Other user-specified value if none of the above apply.

docs.title: 2.5 Machine Learning (ML) Metadata
docs.text:
Version 0.5.0

The metadata for Machine Learning (ML) data (MatCore-ML) is tabulated below. This metadata documents key aspects of the ML method to provide understanding of the dataset generated by it. (Note: This standard inherits the metadata in the minimal MatCore standard, adding the properties below.)

* required appears at most once repeatable

ml-task*

Characterization of the machine learning process performed.

Required Repeatable yes yes type*

The nature of the machine learning task.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes yes — — — —

Legacy: String containing one of the following values: "Property prediction" "Structure prediction" (e.g. crystal structure prediction) "Structure generation" (e.g. de novo crystal generation) "Synthesis prediction" "Material ranking" "Clustering" "Embedding" Other user-specified value if none of the above apply.

Note: This Property can be repeated if the machine learning task involves multiple types of calculations.

description

Explanation of the machine learning task performed.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no — — — —

Legacy: A string containing a more detailed explanation of the machine learning task and its objectives.

ml-model*

A comprehensive description of the machine learning approach and architecture used.

Required Repeatable yes no algorithm*

The machine learning method used.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no — — — —

Legacy: A string containing a description of the machine learning algorithm used (e.g. neural network, random forest, Gaussian process, etc.)

target-variable*

The desired output or answer the machine learning model aims to predict.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes yes — — — —

Legacy: A string containing a description of a target variable the machine learning model aims to predict.

input-feature

Information provided to the machine learning method.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no yes — — — —

Legacy: A string containing a description of the form and meaning of an input variable/feature provided to the machine learning model (e.g. a graph representation of a crystal structure). This can include information on feature engineering performed to define the input (e.g. dimensionality reduction, clustering, etc.).

model-architecture

A description of the network topology used by the specified algorithm.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no — — — —

Legacy: A string containing a description of the model architecture used by the specified algorithm (e.g. for a neural network: the number of layers, nodes per layer, etc.).

model-size

A measure of the magnitude of the machine learning architecture.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no — — — —

Legacy: A string containing a description of the size of the trained model (e.g. number of parameters, storage space, memory requirements, etc.)

training-data

The information used for parameterizing the machine learning model.

Required Repeatable no yes name*

Name of the training dataset used to train in the machine learning model.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no — — — —

Legacy: String containing the dataset name.

contents*

Description of the information included in the training dataset.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no — — — —

Legacy: String containing a description of the training data (e.g. DFT calculations, experiments, etc.)

source

Location from which the training data was obtained.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no — — — —

Legacy: A string containing a MatCore ID, web address, DOI, citation, or other description of the source of the training data.

size

Number of items in the training dataset.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no — — — —

Legacy: A string containing information on the number of data points, configurations, etc., in the training set.

data-preprocessing

Approach used for preliminary refining of raw, unformatted, or incomplete information into a structured and clean state suitable for modeling or analysis.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no — — — —

Legacy: A string containing a description of any preprocessing applied to the dataset to prepare it for training the machine learning model.

missing-data

Documentation of incomplete, null, or unrecorded entries within a feature set that hinder algorithm training.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no — — — —

Legacy: A description of missing entries in the raw dataset (e.g. percentage of missing data and explanation of which fields are missing and why).

missing-data-strategy

Approach used for filling in or removing blank, null, or unknown entries in a dataset.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no — — — —

Legacy: A string describing the approach used for handling missing data.

outlier-handling

Approach to identifying and addressing extreme observations that deviate significantly from the general distribution to ensure they do not disproportionately skew model training.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no — — — —

Legacy: A string containing the method used to detect and handle outliers.

dataset-split

A description of how information used to train the machine learning model was divided into subsets as part of the training process.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no — — — —

Legacy: A string containing information about how the dataset was split into train/validation/test ratios, and any other relevant information related to how the dataset was distributed in the training process.

training-method

The approach used to determine the machine learning model's free parameters.

Required Repeatable no no training-procedure*

The methodology used to determine the machine learning model's free parameters.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no — — — —

Legacy: A string containing a description of the procedure used to train the machine learning model.

training-hyperparameters

Documentation of the settings used in fitting the model.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no — — — —

Legacy: A string describing the hyperparameters used in the training of the model (e.g. learning rate, early-stopping, etc.)

transfer-learning

Method used to migrate knowledge from previously mastered objectives to accelerate proficiency for the current machine learning task.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no — — — —

Legacy: A string containing details of the transfer learning methods used (such as fine-tuning, domain adaptation, multi-task learning, delta learning, etc.).

model-performance

An assessment of the reliability of the machine learning results.

Required Repeatable no no validation*

A description of the approach used to determine the reliability of the obtained machine learning results.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes yes — — — —

The method or process used to identify and measure the range of possible outcomes to assess the reliability of machine learning model predictions.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no — — — —

A technique used to understand the cause-and-effect relationships within the machine learning model's inputs and outputs.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no — — — —

Legacy: A string containing details of the approach and results of the interpretability analysis (e.g. feature importance, global surrogate models, LIME (Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Explanations), SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations), Saliency Maps, etc.)

docs.title: 2.6 Phase Field (PF) Metadata
docs.text:
Version 0.5.0

The metadata for Phase Field (PF) data (MatCore-PF) is tabulated below. This metadata documents key aspects of the PF method to provide understanding of the dataset generated by it. This includes the fundamental mathematical and physical framework governing the PF simulation, including the governing equations, thermodynamic free energy models, and time-evolution state. (Note: This standard inherits the metadata in the minimal MatCore standard, adding the properties below.)

* required appears at most once repeatable

physical-phenomena*

Material process being modeled; description of the overarching processes and mechanisms being modeled/simulated.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes yes — — — —

Legacy: String containing one of the following values: "Isothermal solidification" "Directional solidification" "Isothermal annealing" "Sintering" "Twinning" "Grain growth" "Spinodal decomposition" Other user-specified value if none of the above apply.

problem-specification*

The fundamental mathematical and physical framework governing the phase field simulation, including the governing equations, thermodynamic free energy models, and time-evolution state

Required Repeatable yes no time-dependence*

Description of the time-evolution state targeted by the simulation.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no — — — —

Legacy: String containing one of the following values: "Property prediction" "Transient evolution" "Steady state" "Stationary" "Thermodynamic equilibrium" Other user-specified value if none of the above apply.

governing-equation*

The specific phase field equation used to evolve a field variable.

Required Repeatable yes yes type*

The mathematical classification of the phase field equation.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no — — — —

Legacy: String containing one of the following values: "CH" – Cahn-Hilliard "AC" – Allen-Cahn "GP" – Grand Potential "FID" – Finite Interface Dissipation "PFC" – Phase Field Crystal "Fluid" "Multi" "Coupled" "Diffuse" Other user-specified value if none of the above apply.

evolved-variable*

The name of the field-variable that this equation solves for.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no — — — —

Legacy: A string matching a defined field-variable name (e.g., "phi", "c").

driving-energy

A free energy component that acts as a forcing term in this equation.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no yes — — — —

Legacy: A string matching one of the defined free-energy names (e.g. "f_chem", "f_elastic").

free-energy*

The thermodynamic free energy function used in the system

Required Repeatable yes no name*

The identifier or symbol used for this specific energy functional.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no — — — —

Legacy: A string (e.g., "f_chem", "Chemical Free Energy").

description*

The type/derivation of the thermodynamic bulk free energy function.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no — — — —

Legacy: String containing one of the following values: "Ideal" "Regular" "Flory" "Calphad" "Poly" "Non-polynomial" Other user-specified value if none of the above apply.

expression

The exact mathematical formulation of the phase field functional.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no — — — —

Legacy: A string containing a code snippet, LaTeX formula, or SymPy expression.

unit

docs.title: 2.7 Derived Property Metadata
docs.text:
Version 0.5.0

The metadata for derived properties (MatCore-Der) is tabulated below. This refers to properties computed from data generated using a CMS method documented elsewhere in this section (e.g. spectroscopy computations based on DFT data). (Notes: (1) This standard inherits the metadata in the minimal MatCore standard and one of the associated methods metadata, adding the properties below. (2) Derived properties in this category are limited to properties based on a single method. Derived properties involving a combination of multiple methods (e.g. MD and ML) are not supported. An exception is MBPT, which itself is based on DFT.)

Examples of derived properties include:

  • Electronic (band structure, density of states (DOS), projected DOS, dielectric function, charge and bonding analysis, etc.)
  • Electron-phonon interactions (superconducting properties, line widths, etc.)
  • Linear-response (phonon modes, dispersion, interatomic force constants, vibrational DOS, etc.)
  • Magnetic (magnetics, magnetization, magnons, etc.)
  • Microscopy, electron (S/TEM, 4D-STEM, SAED, etc.)
  • Microscopy, scanning probe (STM, AFM, etc.)
  • NMR (chemical shifts)
  • Optical (electronic excitation spectra, low-loss EELS, etc.)
  • Spectroscopy, core-level (XAS, XES, core-loss EELS, XPS, etc.)
  • Spectroscopy, vibrational (Raman, Infrared spectroscopy, etc.)
  • Transport (electronic conductivity, thermal conductivity, etc.)
  • X-ray scattering (diffraction, reflectivity, pair-distribution function, etc.)

* required appears at most once repeatable

derived-property*

Details of a quantity related to material behavior computed based on a computational materials science (CMS) calculation covered by the MatCore standard.

(2) The Raman tensor is obtained by numerically differentiating the electronic susceptibility with respect to atomic displacements along each vibrational mode and using these tensors to compute Raman scattering intensities for all Raman-active modes, ultimately yielding a full Raman spectrum after appropriate averaging and broadening.</description>

docs.text:
Version 0.5.0

(Normative)

docs.title: I.1 Purpose
docs.text: This annex defines the identifier schemes whose values a MatCore validator checks. An identifier property has two subproperties: value, the identifier itself, and scheme, the name of the scheme it belongs to. The scheme names the rule that value follows.

docs.title: I.2 Rules
docs.text:
1. When scheme is a scheme listed in Table I.1, value SHALL be written in that scheme's form, SHALL match its pattern in full, and SHALL pass its check digit if the scheme has one.
  2. A scheme not listed in Table I.1 is permitted. Its value is not checked, and a validator reports it as user-specified.
  3. Scheme names are written exactly as in Table I.1.
  4. Check digits:
    • ISO/IEC 7064 MOD 11-2: computed over the 16 characters of the identifier, hyphens removed; the last character is the check character, where X stands for 10.
    • ISO/IEC 7064 MOD 97-10 (ROR): the last two digits of a ROR ID are the MOD 97-10 check of the number encoded, in Crockford base 32, by the six characters after the leading 0.
  5. A scheme is added, or its rule changed, only by revision of this annex. Every field of an entry is traced to the scheme's own documentation, named in the Source column.

docs.title: Annex U — MatCore Unit Table
docs.text:
Version 0.5.0

(Normative)

Amended 2026-10-31: Rule 4 extended from generic parameters to any subproperty whose Kind the schema declares as any (decision record 0001).

docs.title: U.1 Purpose
docs.text:
This annex defines the closed set of unit symbols that MAY appear as the value of a unit subproperty in a MatCore metadata instance, the kind of each symbol, and its conversion to coherent SI. It also defines the kind names used in the Kind field of the schema and their mapping to the QUDT ontology.

A validator checks that (a) the symbol is in Table U.4 and (b) its kind matches the kind declared for the property in the schema. No unit parsing is required.

docs.title: U.2 Rules
docs.text:
1. Symbols are case-sensitive ASCII strings. eV and ev are not the same symbol.
  2. Compound symbols use / for division and ^ for integer exponents, exactly as written in Table U.4. Symbols not listed (e.g. eV/A, Å, angstrom**3) are non-conformant.
  3. The reserved symbol dimensionless is used for quantities of dimension one (ratios, counts, fractional coordinates). It SHALL NOT be used for plane angles (use rad or degree) or for amount of substance (use mol).
  4. A unit subproperty of a generic parameter or of any other subproperty whose Kind the schema declares as any MAY, if and only if no symbol in Table U.4 applies, contain a string of the form x-gnu:<expression>, where <expression> is a unit expression valid in GNU Units 2.23 with definitions.units version 3.19 (February 2024). Such values are accepted with a validation warning and are not guaranteed to be machine-convertible. Later versions of definitions.units are not implied; a change of the pinned version is a revision of this annex.
  5. Conversion factors marked exact follow from the SI definitions. Factors marked CODATA 2022 are the 2022 CODATA recommended values published by NIST. The factors in Table U.4 are normative for MatCore and take precedence over the values embedded in any external vocabulary (see Note 5). A revision to a later CODATA release is a revision of this annex.
  6. This annex is versioned with the standard. Instance files SHALL use symbols from the annex version matching their declared MatCore version. Symbols are only ever added; a symbol, once published, is never removed or redefined.
  7. Compatibility between a unit and a kind is decided by the SI dimension vector in Table U.3, not by QUDT's own hasQuantityKind links (see Note 4).
  8. Energy and MolarEnergy are distinct kinds and are not interchangeable. A property declared with Kind Energy SHALL NOT carry a MolarEnergy unit, and vice versa (see Note 1).

Note 1 (molar energies). kJ/mol, kcal/mol and J/mol are units of energy per amount of substance and belong to the kind MolarEnergy, consistent with QUDT, which links these units to quantitykind:MolarEnergy. They are the customary energy units of classical force fields, and properties in the MD section that are conventionally reported per mole are declared with Kind MolarEnergy. Conversion between Energy and MolarEnergy is a division or multiplication by the Avogadro constant (6.022 140 76 × 10²³ mol⁻¹, exact) and is a task for tooling, not for a unit value.

Note 2 (2π convention). InverseLength symbols do not encode whether a factor 2π is included. Properties for which this matters (e.g. k-point-spacing) carry a separate required convention subproperty.

Note 3 (mole vs. dimensionless). Following OPTIMADE, dimensionless SHALL NOT be used for amounts of substance or plane angles.

Note 4 (QUDT quantity-kind links are not a validation basis). The factors in Table U.4 are therefore normative in MatCore (Rule 5) and take precedence over the values embedded in either reference vocabulary.

Note 6 (GNU spelling of bohr). GNU Units does not define bohr; the GNU name is bohrradius. The MatCore symbol remains bohr; the mapping is given in the GNU column.

Note 7 (units absent from QUDT). Ry, bohr, meV, nm^3, 1/ps, 1/bohr, bohr^3, K/angstrom, eV/angstrom^3, hartree/bohr and 1/angstrom^3 have no unit IRI in QUDT Units v3.3.0. For these, the MatCore symbol is the identifier and the quantity-kind IRI in Table U.3 supplies the semantic anchor. QUDT accepts contributions through its public repository, and IRIs will be added to this table if and when they are published.
